prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 (ideological framing removed)

- Economy and tax: Responsible fiscal rules with OBR oversight; repair EU trading relationship; industrial strategy focused on green, digital and biosciences; expand British Business Bank; lifelong skills grants and more apprenticeships; reform apprenticeship levy into a broader skills levy; reverse bank tax cuts, raise Digital Services Tax to 6%, reform capital gains, 4% tax on FTSE-100 buybacks; priority for future income tax cuts by raising the personal allowance; tackle avoidance; financial inclusion strategy.

- Business and work: Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; AI regulatory framework; late payment enforcement; Worker Protection Enforcement Authority; modernise employment status (new “dependent contractor”), zero-hours premium, right to request fixed hours after 12 months; fix Statutory Sick Pay; independent living wage review.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; 10-year home energy upgrade with free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households; zero‑carbon standard for new buildings; rooftop solar incentives; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas; ban fracking and new coal; expand storage, interconnectors and community energy; carbon border adjustment; windfall tax on oil and gas.

- Health: GP access within 7 days (24 hours if urgent) via 8,000 extra GPs and expanded roles for pharmacists/nurses; NHS dentistry access and contract reform; mental health hubs for young people and regular check‑ups; school mental health professional in every school; cancer treatment start within 62 days; public health measures (vaping rules, extended sugar levy); ambulance and hospital estate upgrades; interoperable NHS IT; faster access to medicines (EU recognition); health-led drugs policy and a regulated cannabis market for over‑18s.

- Social care: Free personal care; social care workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers, Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); unpaid carers’ paid leave and respite; National Care Agency and portable care packages.

- Education and skills: Per‑pupil funding rises above inflation; rebuild and repair programme; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; early years boost (extra free hours and higher premium); teacher workforce strategy and independent pay review body; curriculum and vocational reform; SEND funding overhaul; £5,000 lifelong skills grants (aim to £10,000).

- Families and young people: Extend free school meals to all children in poverty; day‑one parental leave/pay rights including self‑employed; higher maternity/shared parental pay and enhanced paternity; “Toddler Top‑Up”; return to Erasmus+; kinship care support.

- Welfare and pensions: Remove two‑child limit and benefit cap; target to end deep poverty with UC adequacy commission; protect triple lock; fair compensation for affected 1950s‑born women; UC first payment in 5 days, scrap bedroom tax, replace sanctions; increase and widen Carer’s Allowance.

- Crime and justice: Community policing; guarantee police attendance for all burglaries; Online Crime Agency; abolish Police and Crime Commissioners; cut court backlogs; improve rehabilitation and probation; modern slavery enforcement; EU data cooperation; fraud reimbursement and transparency.

- Environment/nature: Tougher regulation of water companies (public benefit model, sewage tax, bonus ban), real‑time spill data; binding targets to “double nature” by 2050; plant 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act and agency; protect 30% of land/sea by 2030; deposit return scheme; eliminate non‑recyclable single‑use plastics within three years; peatland and blue carbon restoration.

- Food and farming: National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund Environmental Land Management (+£1bn/year); EU veterinary/plant health agreements; stronger Groceries Code Adjudicator; high welfare and environmental standards in trade; research fund incl. alternative proteins; comprehensive animal welfare bill.

- Housing: 380,000 homes/year including 150,000 social; new garden cities; end no‑fault evictions; three‑year default tenancies; national landlord register; allow councils to end Right to Buy; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding; rent‑to‑own model; end rough sleeping.

- Local government/communities: Multi‑year settlements; powers over second homes/short lets (planning class, up to 500% council tax premium, stamp duty surcharge for overseas buyers of second homes); nationwide gigabit broadband; restore/rationalise bus powers and funding.

- Transport: Accelerate EV rollout (charging points, restore plug‑in grant, 5% VAT on public charging, card access); 2030 zero‑emission sales requirement; freeze rail fares, simplify ticketing; major rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail; £2 bus fare cap and franchising; active travel networks; shift freight to rail; measures to reduce aviation emissions and restrict short flights where rail <2.5h.

- Culture, media, sport: Protect BBC/S4C/Alba/Channel 4; Creative Europe and artist mobility with EU; creative enterprise zones; anti‑SLAPP law; gambling levy, affordability checks, ombudsman; independent football regulator; accessibility quotas for on‑demand TV.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda; 3‑month service standard for claims; allow work after 3 months; expand safe/legal routes; flexible, merit‑based work visas; reverse higher family visa thresholds; protect EU citizens; expand Youth Mobility; Windrush redress; repeal Right to Rent; data‑sharing firewall.

- Rights and equality: Uphold Human Rights Act/ECHR; repeal recent anti‑protest laws; ban conversion practices; misogyny as hate crime; Race Equality Strategy; stronger disability rights and Access to Work reforms; gender recognition reform including non‑binary recognition; assisted dying free vote.

- Political reform and devolution: Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; scrap voter ID; votes at 16; cap donations; Ministerial Code in law; Lords reform; citizens’ assemblies; transparency and lobbying rules; federal approach with enhanced devolved powers and UK Council of Ministers; Barnett protections.

- Defence and international: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; retain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls; procurement reform; improved support for personnel and veterans; deepen European security cooperation; restore 0.7% aid with independent department; support Ukraine (incl. seizing Russian assets); rebuild EU ties via staged roadmap toward Single Market; advocate ceasefire and two‑state solution, recognise Palestine; strengthen human rights sanctions; fund BBC World Service.
